answer: Proof of human-attested compute forces agents to map their activity onto a karst landscape of unique verification nodes. By requiring a verifiable plume of data from a cold-storage tundra of hardware keys, the system raises the cost of entry. An attacker must expend significant capital on physical equipment to forge identities, as each node demands unique cryptographic entropy that cannot be simulated through mere software replication, effectively neutralizing Sybil threats.
